AI Mode reply for vitest useFakeTimers setInterval not advancing

When vi.useFakeTimers() is enabled in Vitest, JavaScript's native timer functions (like setInterval and setTimeout) are paused by design. Time stands perfectly still until you explicitly command it to advance. 
If your setInterval is not advancing or firing, it is usually caused by one of four common pitfalls: 
1. You forgot to manually advance the clock
Because fake timers do not automatically progress, you must tell Vitest to fast-forward the internal clock to trigger the intervals: 
typescript
import { vi, expect, it } from 'vitest';

it('triggers an interval', () => {  vi.useFakeTimers();  let count = 0;  setInterval(() => { count++ }, 1000);  // ❌ Clock is at 0ms. count is still 0  // Move time forward by 2000 milliseconds  vi.advanceTimersByTime(2000); //  // ✅ count is now 2  expect(count).toBe(2); 
});
Use code with caution.
2. Async logic inside the interval (Use the Async methods)
If your setInterval relies on Promises, async/await, or reactive UI updates (like state rendering in React/Vue), the synchronous vi.advanceTimersByTime() finishes before microtasks and DOM updates can flush. 
The Fix: Use the asynchronous version of the timer methods so Vitest can resolve the event loop microtasks: 
typescript
// Use the Async counterpart to let Promises flush
await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(2000);
Use code with caution.
3. Conflict with @testing-library/user-event
If you are simulating user actions (like await user.click()) while fake timers are active, the test will often stall or time out completely. This happens because user-event uses built-in delays that get trapped by Vitest's frozen fake clock. 
The Fix: Configure userEvent to handle fake timers correctly during your setup stage: 
typescript
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';

// Tell userEvent how to advance the clock automatically when it clicks/types
const user = userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers: vi.advanceTimersToNextTimer }); //
Use code with caution.
4. Conflict with MSW (Mock Service Worker)
If you use MSW v2 alongside Vitest's fake timers, MSW's polling logic can freeze or loop infinitely. This is caused by fake timers mocking queueMicrotask by default. 
The Fix: Tell Vitest to skip mocking microtasks when setting up your fake timers: 
typescript
vi.useFakeTimers({  toFake: ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout', 'setInterval', 'clearInterval', 'Date']  // Leave out 'queueMicrotask' and 'process.nextTick'
});
Use code with caution.
To narrow this down, could you tell me: 
  • What framework (React, Vue, Node.js, etc.) are you running this in?
  • Are there any Promises, async operations, or network requests inside your interval?
  • Could you share a brief snippet of your test block?
